project.name: PerfLens
project.goal: Turn PerfLens into a trustworthy production-grade website performance and engineering audit platform whose measurements, classifications, scores, recommendations, reports, and persisted data are evidence-backed, traceable, reproducible, and internally consistent.
definition_of_done: All P0 and P1 tasks pass their acceptance criteria.
No known critical measurement, unit, source, scoring, recommendation, security, or persistence defects remain.
Fresh scans of the regression domains complete without runtime errors.
Backend JSON, database records, frontend presentation, and PDF reports agree on the same underlying results.
Every quantitative claim is traceable to measured evidence or explicitly labeled as a model with assumptions.
No hardcoded domain-specific results, localhost production URLs, fabricated metrics, or fabricated optimization savings remain.
npm test, npm run lint, and npm run build pass.
A final production-readiness report documents remaining limitations and explicitly confirms whether the system is safe to demo and deploy.

product.problem: Existing website audits can produce plausible-looking numbers while hiding unit errors, false positives, unsupported recommendations, inconsistent scoring, source ambiguity, and differences between lab and field measurements.
product.promise: PerfLens should tell a developer what was measured, how it was measured, what evidence supports the finding, how confident the system is, what action is justified, and what improvement can or cannot be quantified.
non_goals: Do not redesign the existing UI/UX.
Do not replace the product with a different architecture without evidence.
Do not optimize for having every metric populated.
Do not imitate Google Lighthouse scores.
Do not claim real-user performance from a single synthetic lab run.
Do not manufacture estimates merely to make reports look complete.

engineering_principles: One source of truth for metric definitions and thresholds.
One canonical internal unit per metric.
Transfer savings are not FCP/LCP savings.
Lab data is not field data.
Frontend and PDF render backend truth; they do not silently recalculate it.
Prefer N/A with an explanation over fabricated data.
Tests must validate real production data paths, not only isolated helper functions.
Fix root causes before downstream symptoms.
Do not mark a task passed without objective acceptance evidence.

tasks.title: Establish audit and baseline
acceptance: Current analyzer architecture is documented.
Current production scan path is traced.
Known historical defects are documented.
Fresh baseline reports are retained for regression comparison.

tasks.title: Fix historical metric and validation defects
acceptance: Historical 1.9s LCP is GOOD.
Historical 7.2s TTI/interactive value cannot become INP.
CLS 0 is valid GOOD data.
Unavailable values do not silently become zero.
Tests cover historical regressions.

tasks.title: Centralize frontend API base URL
acceptance: No hardcoded localhost backend URL remains in src.
API base is centralized.
Tests, lint, and production build pass.

tasks.title: Remove deprecated root MongoDB dependency
acceptance: Confirm whether the deprecated MongoDB package is actually unused.
Remove only if safe.
Server dependencies remain functional.
Install/test/build pass.
No database runtime regression.

tasks.title: Core Web Vitals production correctness
acceptance: LCP is collected from real LCP performance entries.
INP is never sourced from TTI, interactive, TBT, FCP, or arbitrary fallback.
CLS uses real layout-shift data and appropriate session-window logic.
LCP, INP, CLS use canonical units.
Thresholds are centralized and boundary-tested.
Lab and field data are explicit per metric.
Unavailable metrics use null/N/A and do not receive a semantic poor score.
Frontend, API, DB, JSON, and PDF preserve source/mode/value/unit/status/reason.
Fresh scans of google.com, react.dev, github.com, and developer.mozilla.org are captured.
Extreme values such as MDN LCP 21.46s are accompanied by actual evidence before being accepted.
No regression to the historical CWV bugs.

tasks.title: Recommendation engine evidence and estimate correctness
acceptance: Every recommendation originates from a real finding.
Every recommendation contains evidence, category, severity, confidence, and potential impact.
Large JS does not automatically imply unminified, unused, or code-splitting problems.
Unused JS claims require actual coverage/source-map evidence.
Render-blocking JS claims identify actual blocking resources.
TBT recommendations trace to long-task evidence where possible.
LCP recommendations use actual LCP-element evidence.
CLS recommendations identify affected elements where possible.
INP recommendations never use TTI/TBT/FCP as a substitute.
SEO and accessibility recommendations are not represented as performance savings.
Transfer-time estimates are explicitly labeled TRANSFER_ONLY.
No unsupported numeric savings remain.
Measured, modeled, heuristic, transfer-only, and unquantified estimates are distinct.
PDF/JSON/frontend recommendation data match.

tasks.title: Performance analyzer correctness
acceptance: Performance analyzer consumes canonical metric results.
It does not duplicate conflicting threshold logic.
LCP/FCP/TBT/TTFB timing values are traceable to browser data.
Long-task/TBT diagnostics are available when supported.
Timing failures are represented as unavailable rather than zero.
No metric is silently substituted for another.
Performance findings explain their evidence.

tasks.title: SEO and Meta analyzer evidence overhaul
acceptance: Title is checked from rendered DOM.
Meta description is checked from rendered DOM.
Canonical is checked and validated from rendered DOM.
Robots meta and robots.txt are distinguished.
Heading structure is reported without overstating non-errors.
HTML language is checked.
Open Graph metadata is categorized separately from ranking claims.
Relevant internal links are analyzed without inventing crawl results.
Every SEO finding includes selector/raw DOM evidence.
Failed parsing is not treated as missing metadata.
No recommendation is produced without evidence.

tasks.title: Accessibility analyzer correctness
acceptance: Rendered DOM is the source for DOM-level findings.
Missing alt findings identify actual elements.
Form controls have associated accessible names where applicable.
Buttons/links are distinguishable and actionable.
Landmarks and heading structure are evaluated with defensible rules.
ARIA findings are not overgeneralized.
Selectors/evidence are included.
Analyzer does not crash inside page.evaluate due to unavailable server-side helpers.
Accessibility recommendations are not presented as performance savings.

tasks.title: Image optimization analyzer correctness
acceptance: No images is distinguished from image-resource measurement failure.
Actual image URLs, dimensions, formats, transfer sizes, and loading attributes are captured where available.
Natural dimensions versus rendered dimensions are distinguished.
Lazy-loading recommendations require evidence.
Modern-format recommendations require evidence.
Oversized-image recommendations identify affected resources.
Cached/unavailable resource timing is not converted to 0 KB.

tasks.title: JavaScript analyzer correctness
acceptance: Total JS size is measured separately from minification state.
Minification is never inferred solely from payload size.
Unused JS is never inferred from payload size.
Async/defer/module attributes are inspected.
Resource-level evidence is retained.
Compression and transfer sizes are distinguished from source sizes.
Recommendations use measured evidence.

tasks.title: CSS analyzer correctness
acceptance: CSS size is measured correctly.
Minification is not inferred solely from file size.
Render-blocking CSS is identified from actual HTML/resource behavior.
Unused CSS claims require coverage or equivalent evidence.
Critical CSS recommendations require evidence.
Zero-size and unavailable resource timing are distinguished.

tasks.title: Network and waterfall analyzer
acceptance: Requests include URL, type, status, timing, transfer size, cache information where available, and initiator when available.
DNS/TCP/TLS/TTFB timing is not fabricated.
Cached resources are identified where browser evidence permits.
Failed timing entries are represented as unavailable.
Waterfall ordering is consistent with browser timestamps.
Network findings link to actual resources.

tasks.title: Bundle analyzer
acceptance: Bundle/chunk sizes are real.
Compression sizes are distinguished from raw sizes.
Source-map/module analysis is used when available.
Duplicate/unused-module findings require evidence.
No arbitrary unused-code percentage is used.
Recommendations link to actual chunks/modules.

tasks.title: Score analyzer correctness and explainability
acceptance: All score inputs come from canonical metric results.
Unavailable metrics are not treated as poor.
Available metric score 0 remains distinct from unavailable score null.
Weighted contributions are calculated only for available metrics.
Weight normalization is deterministic.
Overall score is bounded to 0-100.
Formula is documented.
PerfLens scores are never labeled as Google Lighthouse scores.
Frontend/PDF show score inputs and contributions sufficiently to audit the result.
Score behavior is tested when metrics are missing.

tasks.title: Cross-analyzer contract and data integrity
acceptance: Every analyzer has a canonical result contract.
Raw value, normalized value, unit, status, source, mode, evidence, reason, and availability are preserved where relevant.
No analyzer silently changes another analyzer's values.
No duplicate/conflicting threshold definitions remain.
JSON, API, DB, frontend, and PDF agree.

tasks.title: Fresh regression and adversarial scan suite
acceptance: Fresh scans cover google.com, react.dev, github.com, developer.mozilla.org, news.ycombinator.com, vercel.com, and at least one additional stable site.
No site-specific hardcoded expectations are used for production calculations.
Same URL scans are repeated enough to detect structural instability.
Expected variance is distinguished from logic errors.
Impossible units, negative values, impossible classifications, and unavailable-as-zero defects are detected.
Stale reports are excluded from validation.

tasks.title: Report and validation integrity
acceptance: PDF is generated from current backend result.
JSON and PDF values match.
Validation reports contain raw evidence and source metadata.
Reports clearly separate CWV from other performance metrics.
Reports distinguish lab from field data.
Report timestamps and analyzer versions are recorded.
No stale report is presented as a fresh scan.

tasks.title: Security and production configuration
acceptance: No frontend secret/service-role credential exposure.
PageSpeed API keys remain server-side.
Production API URL is environment-driven.
CORS, authentication, authorization, and report ownership are validated.
URL scanning prevents unsafe internal/private network targets as appropriate.
SSRF protections are implemented for server-side URL fetching.
Input validation and request limits exist.
Sensitive scan/error data is not leaked.
Production environment does not depend on localhost.

tasks.title: Performance and reliability of PerfLens itself
acceptance: Concurrent scans are bounded.
Browser instances/pages are cleaned up.
Timeouts are explicit.
PageSpeed timeout/fallback behavior is deterministic.
One analyzer failure does not destroy unrelated valid results.
Errors are observable and attached to analyzer diagnostics.
Memory/resource leaks are investigated.

tasks.title: Production deployment validation
acceptance: Production frontend can reach the configured API.
Authentication works in production configuration.
A complete scan works from production UI.
PDF export works.
Supabase persistence works.
History/report retrieval works.
No localhost dependency remains.
Environment variables are documented.

tasks.title: Final clean-room audit
acceptance: Stop all old/stale backend processes.
Start the current production code from a clean state.
Delete or isolate stale validation artifacts.
Run fresh scans.
Compare raw values through the complete pipeline.
Verify frontend/API/DB/PDF consistency.
Verify no hardcoded domain-specific logic.
Run all tests, lint, and build.
Produce FINAL_PRODUCTION_READINESS_REPORT.md.
Do not mark project complete if any P0/P1 acceptance criterion fails.

rules: Read prd.json before every iteration.
Select the highest-priority incomplete task whose prerequisites are satisfied.
Inspect before editing.
Implement the smallest root-cause fix.
Run targeted tests first.
Run full test/lint/build gates after meaningful changes.
Perform fresh runtime validation for analyzer changes.
Only set passes=true after objective acceptance criteria are satisfied.
If a test passes but runtime evidence fails, the task remains incomplete.
If a task reveals a dependency defect, create or update the appropriate prerequisite task rather than masking it.
Never start a later task merely because an earlier task has compilation success.
Never mark a task complete because a report looks plausible.
Never fabricate missing measurements.
Never modify unrelated UI/UX unless required for correctness.
Continue until all required P0/P1 tasks pass or a genuine external blocker is documented.
Before each substantial task, inspect repository state and current PRD status.
Create a concise implementation plan tied directly to acceptance criteria.
Identify affected files and dependencies before editing.
Prefer incremental changes over rewrites.
After implementation, verify the plan against actual behavior.
Record deviations and newly discovered root causes.
Do not treat passing unit tests as proof of browser/runtime correctness.
For analyzer work, require evidence-level validation.
Preserve existing visual identity unless correctness requires a minimal presentation change.
Update documentation and validation artifacts after completing a major analyzer.
